Treat a null `ordertune` as its own type when calculating both means from matched risk/margin records.
Include every non-null `ordertune` found in `orders`, assigning a count of zero to types with no matched risk/margin records, then calculate both means.
Include null `ordertune` as a type alongside every other type found in `orders`, assigning zero counts where applicable, then calculate both means.

queries:
WITH type_counts AS (
    SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS record_count
    FROM riskandmargin AS r
    JOIN orders AS o ON o.recordvault = r.ordervault
    WHERE o.ordertune IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(record_count) AS mean_count
    FROM type_counts
)
SELECT
    AVG(t.record_count) AS mean_count,
    AVG(t.record_count - m.mean_count) AS mean_excess
FROM type_counts AS t
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS m
WHERE t.record_count > m.mean_count

SELECT
    ordertune,
    SUM(CASE WHEN dealedge = 'Buy' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS buy_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN dealedge = 'Sell' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sell_count,
    AVG(dealquote) AS mean_dealquote,
    AVG(dealcount) AS mean_dealcount
FROM orders
GROUP BY ordertune

WITH order_types(ordertune) AS (
    VALUES ('Stop'), ('Market'), ('Limit'), ('StopLimit')
),
types AS (
    SELECT ordertune FROM order_types
    UNION ALL
    SELECT NULL
    WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE ordertune IS NULL)
)
SELECT
    t.ordertune,
    COUNT(o.orderspivot) AS order_count,
    AVG(o.dealquote) AS mean_dealquote,
    AVG(o.dealcount) AS mean_dealcount
FROM types AS t
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.ordertune IS t.ordertune
GROUP BY t.ordertune
